events.title: Battle of Ayacucho
events.description: Forces led by Antonio José de Sucre defeated the Spanish royalist army at Ayacucho in the Andes of Peru, the last major battle of the South American wars of independence.
events.significance: The victory effectively ended Spanish colonial rule in South America and secured the independence of Peru and the surrounding region.

events.title: First Traffic Signal Installed in London
events.description: A gas-lit traffic signal designed by railway engineer John Peake Knight was installed outside the Houses of Parliament in Westminster to control horse-drawn carriage traffic.
events.significance: It was one of the first traffic signals in the world and a forerunner of modern traffic control systems, though it was removed after a gas explosion injured a police officer in 1869.

events.title: First Episode of Coronation Street Airs
events.description: The British soap opera Coronation Street, set in the fictional Weatherfield, made its debut on ITV in the UK.
events.significance: It became the longest-running television soap opera in the world and a major influence on British popular culture and TV drama.

events.title: UN Adopts the Genocide Convention
events.description: The United Nations General Assembly approved the Convention on the Prevention and Punishment of the Crime of Genocide, defining genocide as an international crime.
events.significance: It established genocide as a crime under international law and laid the legal foundation for later international tribunals and prosecutions.

events.title: Smallpox Eradication Certified
events.description: A global commission of scientists certified that smallpox had been eradicated worldwide, and the World Health Assembly formally declared it in 1980.
events.significance: Smallpox remains the only human infectious disease to be completely eradicated, a landmark achievement in public health and vaccination.
